mainTopic: Misleading buyers by dressing up goods (end of פרק הזהב), and the start of the laws of interest: נשך and תרבית
overview: This amud first finishes the laws of misleading a buyer. The חכמים who allow sifting beans are identified as רבי אחא, who permits a change the buyer can plainly see. A ברייתא lists forbidden tricks that make animals and meat look better than they are. Several אמוראים allowed decorating goods, and the גמרא reconciles this with the משנה: new goods may be decorated, but old goods may not. A story about an old slave who dyed his hair shows what adorning a person means. After the Hadran for פרק הזהב, a new chapter opens with a משנה defining נשך and תרבית, the two Torah words for interest. The גמרא tries to find a case of one without the other, and רבא concludes that they always come together, so every loan with interest breaks two לאוין. A ברייתא then shows from the פסוקים that both נשך and ריבית apply to money and to food.

steps.title: Why lowering prices is a good thing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its explanation from just before: the seller who lowers his prices is praised because he brings down the market price.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because he makes the market rate easier for everyone.
steps.whatsHappening: This line is the end of an answer that began just before. It explains why חכמים praise a seller who sells below the going price.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Other sellers may be annoyed when one seller lowers his price, but the public gains from it. His low price pulls the whole market price down, so the חכמים see it as a good deed.

phrases.english: Because he eases the market rate.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the explanation started at the end of the previous section.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Lowering prices brings down the whole market rate, which helps the public.

steps.title: The משנה about sifting ground beans
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: אבא שאול forbids sifting ground beans, and the חכמים permit it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And one may not sift ground beans; these are the words of אבא שאול. And the חכמים permit it, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new line of the משנה so it can discuss it. This sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אבא שאול is worried that sifting out the waste lets the seller charge more and gives a false picture of the goods. The חכמים allow it. The next step asks who these חכמים are.

phrases.english: And he may not sift the ground beans,
these are the words of Abba Shaul.
And the Rabbis permit it, etc.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next ruling in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אבא שאול forbids sifting ground beans; the חכמים permit it.

steps.title: Who are these חכמים?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which specific תנא the משנה means by 'חכמים'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who are the חכמים?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wants to know who stands behind the anonymous 'חכמים' in the משנה. It is setting up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Knowing who the חכמים are tells us the reason behind their view. That reason also tells us how far their permission goes.

phrases.english: Who are the Rabbis?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the חכמים quoted in step 2.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The identity of the חכמים who permit sifting.

steps.title: It is רבי אחא, who allows a change the buyer can see
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים are רבי אחא. A ברייתא teaches that he permits such changes when the change is easy to see.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is רבי אחא, as a ברייתא teaches: רבי אחא permits it in something where the change can be seen.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the חכמים are רבי אחא. It proves this with a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אחא's reason is that the buyer can see the sifted beans with his own eyes. If the buyer knows what he is paying extra for, nobody is being fooled.
steps.whatToRemember: Sifting is allowed according to רבי אחא because the buyer can see the change, so he is not tricked.

phrases.english: It is Rabbi Aḥa, as it is taught:
Rabbi Aḥa permits it in an item where it is visible.
phrases.notes: 'It is visible' means the buyer can plainly see the improvement, so he knows what he is paying for.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The חכמים are רבי אחא, who permits a change that can be seen.

steps.title: The משנה: no dressing up people, animals or goods
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה that forbids making a person, an animal or goods look better than they are in order to sell them.
steps.simpleTranslation: One may not adorn a person, and so on, nor goods.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה to discuss it. A ברייתא with more examples follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Decorating something for sale can hide its faults and fool the buyer. That is why the משנה forbids it.

keyTerms.meaning: adorn, dress up to look better

phrases.aramaic: אֵין מְפַרְכְּסִין, לֹא אֶת הָאָדָם וְכוּ׳
phrases.english: One may not adorn, not a person, etc.
phrases.notes: 'Person' here means a slave being sold.

phrases.english: and not the goods.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next ruling in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: It is forbidden to adorn people, animals or goods for sale.

steps.title: A ברייתא: tricks with animals and meat
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lists three forbidden tricks: stiffening an animal's hair, blowing air into innards, and soaking meat in water.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: one may not stiffen an animal's hair, one may not blow air into innards, and one may not soak meat in water.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with practical examples of the forbidden 'dressing up'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each trick makes the item look bigger or better than it really is. Stiff hair makes an animal look fuller, air makes innards look larger, and water changes the color of meat.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
One may not stiffen the hair of an animal,
and one may not inflate innards,
and one may not soak meat in water.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אֵין מְשַׁרְבְּטִין אֶת הַבְּהֵמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds examples to the משנה in step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Stiffening an animal's hair, inflating innards and soaking meat are all forbidden.

steps.title: What does 'משרבטין' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the unclear word משרבטין means.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is 'one may not stiffen'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to explain a hard word from the ברייתא. Two answers follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word is unusual, so the גמרא needs to know exactly which action is being forbidden.

phrases.english: What is: One may not stiffen?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about a word from the ברייתא in step 6.

steps.title: First explanation: feeding bran water
steps.stepSummary: In בבל they explained that it means giving the animal bran water to drink.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here they explained it as bran water.
steps.whatsHappening: The first answer: משרבטין means feeding the animal bran water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Bran water swells the animal's belly and makes its hair stand up. That makes the animal look fatter and healthier than it really is.

phrases.english: Here they explained:
phrases.notes: 'Here' means in בבל, where this גמרא was taught.

phrases.english: Bran water.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 7.

steps.title: Second explanation: scrubbing the hair
steps.stepSummary: זעירי, in the name of רב כהנא, says it means scrubbing the hair so it stands up.
steps.simpleTranslation: זעירי said in the name of רב כהנא: scrubbing.
steps.whatsHappening: A second, different explanation of the same word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the trick is done on the outside: scrubbing the hair makes it stand up and look fuller. Both explanations agree on the purpose, which is making the animal look bigger. They differ only on how it is done.

keyTerms.meaning: scrubbing the hair so it stands up

phrases.english: Ze'eiri said in the name of Rav Kahana:
Scrubbing the hair to make it stand up.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different answer from step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Scrubbing the hair so it stands up.

steps.title: אמוראים who allowed decorating goods
steps.stepSummary: Five אמוראים allowed sellers to decorate clothing and baskets in different ways.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל allowed putting fringes on a cloak. רב יהודה allowed cleaning decorated garments. רבה allowed beating linen garments. רבא allowed drawing arrow patterns. רב פפא בר שמואל allowed drawing basket patterns.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא lists cases where אמוראים allowed decorating goods for sale. This sets up a contradiction with the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All these cases make goods look nicer, which seems to be exactly what the משנה forbids. The question comes in the next step.

phrases.english: Shmuel permitted putting fringes on a cloak.
Rav Yehuda permitted cleaning ornamented garments.
Rabba permitted beating linen garments to make them look finer.
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets; the word in square brackets is the corrected wording.

phrases.english: Rava permitted drawing arrow patterns.
Rav Pappa bar Shmuel permitted
drawing basket patterns.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings rulings that seem to go against the משנה in step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Several אמוראים allowed decorating clothing and baskets for sale.

steps.title: But the משנה forbids decorating
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges these rulings from the משנה, which forbids adorning people, animals or goods.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we learned in the משנה: one may not adorn a person, an animal or goods!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that these permissions seem to go directly against the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה clearly includes 'goods' (כלים) in the ban. So how could the אמוראים allow decorating clothing and baskets?

keyTerms.meaning: but didn't we learn in the משנה?

phrases.english: But didn't we learn:
One may not adorn a person,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא אֶת הַבְּהֵמָה, וְלֹא אֶת הַכֵּלִים!
phrases.english: nor an animal, nor goods!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the rulings in step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rulings of the אמוראים that allowed decorating goods.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה forbids adorning goods, and these rulings allow exactly that.

steps.title: New goods versus old goods
steps.stepSummary: There is no contradiction: decorating new goods is allowed, and decorating old goods is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult: this is about new items, and that is about old items.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the contradiction by splitting the cases into new goods and old goods.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Decorating a new item only brings out its real beauty, so the buyer is not fooled. Decorating an old item hides its wear and makes it look new, and that is the deception the משנה forbids.
steps.whatToRemember: Decorating is forbidden only when it hides a flaw, as with old goods. Making new goods look nice is allowed.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
This is with new items, that is with old items.
phrases.notes: 'This' means the אמוראים's permissions, which are about new goods; 'that' means the משנה's ban, which is about old goods.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: הָא בְּחַדְתֵי, הָא בְּעַתִּיקֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 11.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any decorating is forbidden, so the אמוראים contradict the משנה.
steps.terutzMaskana: New goods may be decorated; old goods may not, because decorating them hides their flaws.

steps.title: What does adorning a person mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the משנה means by פרכוס of a person.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is 'adorning' a person?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא has explained adorning animals and goods. Now it asks what adorning a person means, and the answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה listed three things you may not adorn for sale: people, animals and goods. Animals and goods were already explained, so only the person case is left. This question sets up a story that shows the case.

keyTerms.meaning: Adorning or dressing something up so it looks better than it really is
A person (here, a slave being sold)

phrases.english: Adornment of a person, what is it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from adorning goods (steps 10 to 12) to the last case in the משנה, adorning a person.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A concrete example of what it means to adorn a person for sale.

steps.title: The old slave dyes his hair and goes to רבא
steps.stepSummary: An old עבד dyed his hair and beard to look young and asked רבא to buy him. רבא refused.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is like the case of a certain old slave who dyed his head and beard. He came before רבא and said, 'Buy me!' רבא said to him, 'Let the poor be the members of your household.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a story. An old slave dyed his hair black to look younger so someone would buy him, and רבא turned him down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Dyeing white hair black is the example of adorning a person: it hides the slave's real age from a buyer. רבא declined by quoting a known saying. He did not need a slave because the poor people in his home could help him.

keyTerms.meaning: Let the poor be members of your household

phrases.english: Like that case of a certain old slave,
who went and dyed his head and his beard.
He came before Rava,
he said to him: Buy me!

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: יִהְיוּ עֲנִיִּים בְּנֵי בֵיתֶךָ.
phrases.english: He said to him: Let the poor be members of your household.
phrases.notes: רבא is quoting a known saying of the חכמים. He means he doesn't need a slave, because poor people in his home can help him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 13's question with a story.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Adorning a person means something like an old slave dyeing his hair to hide his age from a buyer.

steps.title: רב פפא בר שמואל buys the slave and discovers the trick
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא בר שמואל bought the slave. When asked for water, the slave whitened his hair again and said he was older than רב פפא's father.
steps.simpleTranslation: He came before רב פפא בר שמואל, who bought him. One day רב פפא said to him, 'Give me water to drink!' The slave went and whitened his head and beard. He said to him, 'See, I am older than your father.'
steps.whatsHappening: The story goes on. The slave got bought by רב פפא בר שמואל, and then showed his real age so he would not have to work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This part shows why adorning a person is a real deception. The buyer paid for a young worker and got an old man who would not serve. The trick only came out after the sale.

phrases.aramaic: אֲתָא לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב פָּפָּא בַּר שְׁמוּאֵל, זַבְנֵיהּ.
phrases.english: He came before Rav Pappa bar Shmuel, who bought him.
One day he said to him: Give me water to drink!
He went and whitened his head and his beard.
He said to him: See that I am older than your father.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲתָא לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב פָּפָּא בַּר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the slave story after רבא refused him.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The slave's dyed hair fooled the buyer, which shows how adorning a person cheats the buyer.

steps.title: רב פפא applies a פסוק to himself
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא בר שמואל quoted the פסוק 'The righteous is delivered from trouble, and another comes in his place' about himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: He read about himself: 'The righteous one is delivered from trouble, and another comes in his place.'
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends with רב פפא admitting what happened by quoting a פסוק from משלי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'righteous one' who escaped the trouble is רבא, who refused to buy the slave. רב פפא saw himself as the 'another' who got stuck with the problem instead.
steps.whatToRemember: Adorning a person means hiding his real condition, like dyeing an old slave's hair, so a buyer pays for something he is not really getting.

phrases.english: He read about himself:
The righteous one is delivered from trouble,
phrases.notes: משלי 11:8. Here 'the righteous one' is רבא, who got out of buying the slave.

phrases.english: and another comes in his place.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the slave story with רב פפא's comment on it.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבא escaped the deception and רב פפא was caught by it, which closes the explanation of adorning a person.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing פרק הזהב
steps.stepSummary: The closing formula for the chapter הזהב.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, הזהב.
steps.whatsHappening: This line marks the end of the fourth פרק of בבא מציעא, called הזהב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Hadran is not part of the argument. It is a traditional farewell to the chapter that was just finished.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you (said when finishing a chapter)
'The gold', the name of this chapter

phrases.english: We will return to you, HaZahav.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Formally closes the chapter after the last story.

steps.title: New chapter: what are נשך and תרבית?
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה opens by asking what counts as נשך and what counts as תרבית, the two Torah words for interest.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Which is נשך, and which is תרבית?
steps.whatsHappening: A new chapter begins with a משנה about the ban on taking interest. It opens by asking for definitions of the two words the Torah uses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah uses two different words for interest, נשך and תרבית. The משנה asks what each one means. This sets up the definitions that come next, starting with lending a סלע to be paid back as five דינרים.

keyTerms.meaning: Increase, another Torah word for interest

steps.confusionAlert: The משנה asks about נשך and תרבית separately, but don't conclude that they are two different kinds of interest. The גמרא later concludes, in the name of רבא (step 29), that by Torah law they always come together. The two names just add a second לאו.
steps.whyThisMatters: This question opens the whole chapter on the laws of ריבית, interest between Jews.

phrases.english: MISHNA: Which is neshekh,
phrases.notes: Both words come from the Torah's ban on interest, ויקרא 25:36–37.

phrases.english: and which is tarbit?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a brand-new chapter and topic after the Hadran.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה sets out to define the two Torah words for forbidden interest, נשך and תרבית.

steps.title: Defining נשך: paying back more than you borrowed
steps.stepSummary: The משנה defines נשך as lending something and getting back more of it, such as a סלע for five דינרים or two סאה of wheat for three.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is נשך? Someone who lends a סלע and gets back five דינרים, or lends two סאה of wheat and gets back three. This is forbidden, because he 'bites' the borrower.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה answers the first half of its opening question and gives a clear example of נשך.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A סלע is worth four דינרים, so getting five back is one extra דינר. The same works with wheat: lend two, collect three. The word נשך comes from 'biting', because the lender takes a bite out of the borrower's money.

keyTerms.meaning: A silver coin; four make a סלע
A measure of volume for grain

phrases.english: What is נשך?
One who lends a סלע to get back five דינרים,
phrases.notes: A סלע is worth four דינרים, so the lender gets one extra.

phrases.english: or two סאה of wheat to get back three,
this is forbidden, because he 'bites' the borrower.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the first half of the question asked in step 18
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Lending with a set extra repayment, whether in money or in produce, is forbidden as נשך.

steps.title: Defining תרבית: setting up the wheat case
steps.stepSummary: The משנה starts its example of תרבית. Someone buys wheat at the market price of one gold דינר per כור, and later the price of wheat rises to thirty.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is תרבית? It is making a profit through produce. How so? He bought wheat from him at one gold דינר per כור, which was the market price. Then wheat went up to thirty דינרים.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה turns to תרבית and sets up a sale case. It is laying out the facts that the next step will finish.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A gold דינר equals 25 silver דינרים, so the buyer paid 25 per כור. That was the fair price at the time, so the sale itself is fine. The trouble only starts later, after the price climbs to 30.

keyTerms.meaning: A gold דינר, worth 25 silver דינרים

phrases.english: And what is תרבית?
One who makes an increase through produce.
How so?
He bought wheat from him
at a gold דינר per כור,
and that was the market price.
Then wheat went up to thirty דינרים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the second half of the step 18 question by setting up the case
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets up the facts: a fair sale of wheat at 25, after which the price rises to 30.

steps.title: The wheat debt becomes a wine debt the seller does not own
steps.stepSummary: The buyer asks for his wheat so he can buy wine. The seller instead credits him thirty per כור toward wine, but the seller has no wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: The buyer said: Give me my wheat, because I want to sell it and buy wine. The seller said: I count your wheat as worth thirty, and I owe you wine for that amount. But the seller has no wine.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes the תרבית case. It shows how a fair wheat sale turns into a wine debt that can bring the buyer extra profit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wheat debt is turned into a debt of wine at today's value. The seller owns no wine, so if wine goes up he has to pay back more than he owed. That extra gain for the buyer is the 'increase' called תרבית.

keyTerms.meaning: Are set on me; counted as my debt

steps.confusionAlert: The original sale was completely fine. The problem is turning the wheat debt into a wine debt when the seller owns no wine.

phrases.english: He said to him: Give me my wheat,
because I want to sell it
and buy wine with it.
He said to him: Your wheat
is counted against me at thirty,
and you have wine with me for that amount,
and he has no wine.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ: תֵּן לִי חִטַּי, שֶׁאֲנִי רוֹצֶה לְמוֹכְרָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the case begun in step 20
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Turning a produce debt into a debt of wine at a fixed value, when the seller has no wine, is תרבית.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה shows נשך through a simple loan, and shows תרבית through a sale that turns into a wine debt.

steps.title: Inference: on a Torah level, נשך and תרבית are one thing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that the משנה explains תרבית using a rabbinic case and skips Torah-level interest. From this it infers that by Torah law נשך and תרבית are the same prohibition.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה skipped over Torah-level ריבית and explained a rabbinic case. That shows that, by Torah law, נשך and תרבית are one and the same.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by drawing a conclusion from how the משנה chose its examples.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wine case is a sale, not a loan, so it is only forbidden מדרבנן. If Torah-level תרבית were its own separate thing, the משנה should have given an example of it. Since it didn't, Torah-level נשך and תרבית must be one prohibition.

keyTerms.meaning: By inference; we can learn from this

phrases.english: גמרא:
Since he leaves aside Torah-level interest,
and explains a rabbinic case instead,
we can learn that by Torah law,
נשך and תרבית are one and the same thing.
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the letter ד in round brackets. The meaning stays the same.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִדְּשָׁבֵיק לְרִיבִּית דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא, וְקָא מְפָרֵשׁ דְּרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a conclusion from how the משנה chose its examples
steps.mimraCoreRuling: By Torah law, נשך and תרבית are a single prohibition.

steps.title: Challenge: the פסוק seems to split them into money and food
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the inference. The פסוק uses נשך for money and ריבית for food, which makes them look like two separate things.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the פסוקים say 'נשך of money' and 'ריבית of food', so they look like two different things!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the conclusion of step 22 using the wording of the Torah.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If נשך and תרבית were one thing, why would the Torah link one word to money and the other to food? The split wording suggests two separate categories. That goes against the claim that they are the same.

phrases.english: But the פסוקים are written:
נשך with money, and ריבית with food!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the inference of step 22
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that by Torah law נשך and תרבית are one thing
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק links נשך to money and ריבית to food. That looks like two separate categories.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the גמרא's next look at whether נשך can exist without תרבית, or תרבית without נשך.

steps.title: Could you really have one without the other?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back on the challenge. Do you really think נשך can exist without תרבית, or תרבית without נשך?
steps.simpleTranslation: And do you really think there is נשך without תרבית, and תרבית without נשך?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 23 with a pointed question: can you even picture one of these without the other? This sets up the test cases that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge said the פסוק uses two different words, so they must be two different kinds of interest. The גמרא replies that two words do not prove two separate kinds of interest unless a real case exists where only one of them applies. It will now look for such a case.

keyTerms.meaning: And do you really think? A word that pushes back on an assumption
Literally 'biting.' Interest seen as the borrower's loss
Literally 'increase.' Interest seen as the lender's gain

phrases.english: And do you really think there is נשך without תרבית,
and תרבית without נשך?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 23 by doubting that the two can ever be separated.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rhetorical rejection of the assumption behind the challenge
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Two different words in the פסוק mean two separate kinds of interest, one for money and one for food.
steps.terutzMaskana: No real case of one without the other exists, so by Torah law they are one thing that is always found together (רבא later explains the two names as two לאוין).

steps.title: A possible case of נשך without תרבית
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what נשך without תרבית would look like. It suggests a loan of 100 coins repaid with 120, where the coins dropped in value so that 120 are now worth what 100 used to be worth.
steps.simpleTranslation: What would נשך without תרבית look like? Say he lent him 100 coins to be repaid with 120. At first, 100 coins were worth a sixth of a דינר, and in the end 120 coins were worth a sixth of a דינר. There is נשך, because the lender 'bites' him by taking something he did not give. There is no תרבית, because the lender gains nothing: he lent a sixth of a דינר and got back a sixth of a דינר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the idea by suggesting a case where only נשך seems to apply. The borrower hands over more coins, but the lender ends up with the same value.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case splits the two ideas apart. Counting coins, the borrower pays extra, which looks like 'biting.' Measuring value, the lender's wealth did not grow, so it looks like there is no 'increase.'

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? What would it look like?

phrases.english: What would נשך without תרבית look like?
If he lent him 100 to be repaid with 120,
and at first 100 were worth a sixth of a דינר,
and in the end 120 were worth a sixth of a דינר.
There is נשך, because he 'bites' him,

phrases.aramaic: דְּקָא שָׁקֵיל מִינֵּיהּ מִידֵּי דְּלָא יָהֵיב.
phrases.english: since he takes from him something he did not give.
And there is no תרבית, because he has no profit,
since he lent him a sixth of a דינר
and he takes back a sixth of a דינר from him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the claim from step 24 by proposing a real case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is there a real case of נשך without תרבית?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A suggested case: coins that drop in value, so more coins are repaid for the same worth. The next step rejects it.

steps.title: The case falls apart
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the case. If you judge by the value at the time of the loan, there is both נשך and תרבית. If you judge by the value at the time of repayment, there is neither.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the end, if you go by the start, there is נשך and there is תרבית. If you go by the end, there is no נשך and no תרבית.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the suggested case does not really split נשך from תרבית. It mixed two different moments of time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case counted coins to find נשך and measured value to find no תרבית. But you have to pick one point in time. At the time of the loan, 120 is more than 100, so both are present. At repayment, the value is equal, so neither is present.

keyTerms.meaning: You go by the starting point

steps.whatToRemember: נשך and תרבית rise and fall together. Judged at any one moment, either both are there or neither is.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix time frames. The false case only worked because it judged נשך at one moment and תרבית at another.

phrases.english: In the end,
if you go by the start,
phrases.notes: He means the coins' value on the day of the loan.

phrases.english: there is נשך and there is תרבית.
If you go by the end,

phrases.aramaic: לָא נֶשֶׁךְ אִיכָּא וְלָא תַּרְבִּית אִיכָּא.
phrases.english: there is no נשך and there is no תרבית.

steps.triggerLanguage: סוֹף סוֹף, אִי בָּתַר מֵעִיקָּרָא אָזְלַתְּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the case suggested in step 25.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggested case of נשך without תרבית
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It judged the two at different moments. At any single moment, both are present or both are absent.

steps.title: A possible case of תרבית without נשך
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what תרבית without נשך would look like. It suggests a loan of 100 coins repaid with 100, where the coins rose in value from a sixth of a דינר to a fifth.
steps.simpleTranslation: And more: what would תרבית without נשך look like? Say he lent 100 to be repaid with 100. At first, 100 were worth a sixth of a דינר, and in the end 100 were worth a fifth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins the reverse test. Here the coin count is equal, but the value went up. The גמרא is setting up a case that it will test next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Counting coins, the borrower pays nothing extra, so it looks like no 'biting.' Measuring value, the lender gains, so it looks like 'increase.' The same timing problem as in step 26 is about to be raised.

phrases.aramaic: וְתוּ, תַּרְבִּית בְּלֹא נֶשֶׁךְ הֵיכִי דָמֵי?
phrases.english: And more: what would תרבית without נשך look like?
If he lent 100 to be repaid with 100,
and at first 100 were worth a sixth of a דינר,
and in the end 100 were worth a fifth.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתוּ, תַּרְבִּית בְּלֹא נֶשֶׁךְ הֵיכִי דָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting the first case, the גמרא tests the reverse case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is there a real case of תרבית without נשך?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A suggested case: coins that rise in value, repaid at the same count. The rejection comes in the next lines.

steps.title: The Case of Coins Rising in Value Fails Too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the case of 100 coins repaid with 100 after they rose in value. Judged by the value at the time of the loan there is neither prohibition, and judged by the value at repayment there are both.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you go by the original value, there is no נשך and no תרבית. If you go by the final value, there is both נשך and תרבית!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the case it just suggested for תרבית without נשך, the same way it knocked down the earlier case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The borrower returned the same number of coins, so by the original value he paid nothing extra and there is no interest at all. By the value at repayment he paid more than he got, so there is both a 'bite' and an 'increase.' Either way, the two prohibitions show up together or not at all.

keyTerms.meaning: From the start: the value at the time of the loan
The end: the value at the time of repayment
You go (by): which point in time you measure from

phrases.english: If you go by the original value,

phrases.aramaic: לָא נֶשֶׁךְ אִיכָּא וְלָא תַּרְבִּית אִיכָּא.
phrases.english: there is no נשך and there is no תרבית.
If you go by the final value,
then there is נשך and there is תרבית!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the case proposed in step 27, mirroring the rejection in step 26.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proposed case of תרבית without נשך (coins rising in value).
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Measured at either point in time, the two prohibitions always go together, so this is not a case of one without the other.

steps.title: רבא: The Two Always Go Together, So There Are Two Prohibitions
steps.stepSummary: רבא concludes that נשך and תרבית never exist apart. The פסוק names them separately only so that taking interest breaks two לאוין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: You never find נשך without תרבית, or תרבית without נשך. The פסוק split them only so that the lender breaks two negative commandments.
steps.whatsHappening: After both cases failed, רבא gives the final answer: the two names describe one thing, and the תורה lists them separately to add a second לאו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 23 argued from the פסוק that נשך and תרבית are two different things. Steps 24 to 28 then tested cases of one without the other, and each case failed. רבא concludes that they are really one: the separate wording in the פסוק does not create separate cases, it doubles the prohibition for every case of interest.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather: drops the earlier approach and brings a new one
The פסוק divided them, naming them separately
To make him break it, so he is in violation

steps.whatToRemember: נשך and תרבית are one thing with two names. Every loan with interest breaks two לאוין.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think נשך and תרבית are two kinds of interest. According to רבא, every interest case is both at once.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the rule for the whole topic: any interest at all counts as both prohibitions, and that is the base for the ברייתא that follows.

phrases.english: Rather, רבא said:

phrases.aramaic: אִי אַתָּה מוֹצֵא לֹא נֶשֶׁךְ בְּלֹא תַּרְבִּית,
phrases.english: You do not find נשך without תרבית,
nor תרבית without נשך.
And the verse distinguished between them only
so that he violates two prohibitions.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Since both cases were rejected, רבא resolves the challenge from step 23 by explaining why the פסוק uses two names.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: נשך and תרבית are always found together; the תורה names them separately so that interest breaks two לאוין.

steps.title: ברייתא: The Basic Reading of the Verse
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes the פסוק in ויקרא, which links נשך with money and מרבית with food. From that פסוק alone, we would know only those two pairings.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: 'Do not give him your money with נשך, and do not give your food with מרבית.' From this I know only נשך with money and ריבית with food.
steps.whatsHappening: A new source, a ברייתא, starts here. It reads the simple meaning of the פסוק and sets up the questions that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in ויקרא pairs each word with one item: נשך goes with money and מרבית goes with food. The phrase 'אין לי אלא' tells us the ברייתא wants to stretch each prohibition to the other item as well.

keyTerms.meaning: Increase: another form of the word תרבית or ריבית
I have only: from this source I would know only this much

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
"You shall not give him your money with neshekh,
and with marbit you shall not give your food."
I have only neshekh with money
and ribit with food.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new ברייתא about which items each prohibition covers.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Read simply, the פסוק in ויקרא teaches נשך with money and ריבית with food.

steps.title: Where Do We Learn נשך With Food?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks for a source that the prohibition of נשך also applies to a loan of food.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know that there is נשך with food?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks its first question: how do we know that נשך also covers food?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in ויקרא tied נשך only to money. The ברייתא wants a separate source that applies it to food too.

keyTerms.meaning: From where? Asks for a source in the פסוק

phrases.english: From where do we know neshekh with food?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from the limit stated with 'אין לי אלא.'
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that נשך applies to food.

steps.title: The Verse Says 'נשך אכל'
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא answers from the פסוק in דברים, which says 'נשך אכל,' the נשך of food.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'נשך of food.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers with a different פסוק that puts the word נשך right next to food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in דברים lists items covered by נשך, and food is one of them. So נשך is not limited to money.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק teaches: introduces the source

phrases.english: The verse states: "Neshekh of food."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 31.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The words 'נשך אכל' in דברים show that נשך applies to food.

steps.title: Where Do We Learn ריבית With Money?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks for a source that the prohibition of ריבית also applies to a loan of money.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know that there is ריבית with money?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks the mirror question: how do we know that ריבית also covers money?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in ויקרא tied מרבית only to food. Now the ברייתא wants a source that applies it to money as well.

keyTerms.meaning: ריבית on a loan of money

phrases.english: From where do we know ribit with money?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallels the question of step 31, this time for ריבית.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that ריבית applies to money.

steps.title: The Verse Says 'נשך כסף'
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא answers from the words 'נשך כסף' in the פסוק in דברים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'נשך of money.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא brings the words 'נשך כסף' as its source for ריבית with money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We already knew נשך with money from ויקרא, so the words 'נשך כסף' in דברים seem to say nothing new about נשך. The ברייתא therefore uses them to teach ריבית with money.
steps.whatToRemember: With both answers together, נשך and ריבית each apply to money and to food alike.
steps.confusionAlert: Notice the answer quotes the word נשך even though the question was about ריבית. That is on purpose: the words 'נשך כסף' are repeated, so they are put to use for ריבית.

phrases.english: The verse states: "Neshekh of money."
phrases.notes: דברים 23:20, the same פסוק as before.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 33.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The words 'נשך כסף' in דברים are the source that ריבית applies to money.
